draft.title: From cells to organ systems
card: a group of similar cells that do the same job. Muscle tissue is one example.
a structure made of different tissues that work together to do a particular job. The stomach is an organ.
a group of organs that work together to carry out a major job for the body. The organs of the digestive system work together to deal with food.
Cells, tissues, organs and organ systems build up in that order. Together the organ systems keep the whole organism alive.
draft.remember: Each level is built from the one below it, and the levels work as a team.

a.q: Which list shows the levels of organisation from smallest to largest?
a.why: Similar cells make a tissue, different tissues make an organ, and organs make an organ system. Putting organ before tissue is tempting, but an organ is built from several tissues, so it is larger.
a.clue: Start with the smallest unit and ask what it forms.

b.q: The heart contains muscle tissue, nerve tissue and connective tissue, and it pumps blood. Why is the heart an organ and not a tissue?
opts: It is made of different tissues working together
It is made of one type of cell doing one job
It is a group of organs doing a major body job
It is made of cells, and tissues have no cells
b.why: An organ is made of different tissues that work together for a particular job. A tissue is made of similar cells, so a structure with several tissue types is not a tissue. It is not an organ system either, because it is one organ and not a group of organs.
b.clue: Count how many types of tissue the heart has.

b.best: It is made of different tissues working together
